rows.description: The child has learned she always comes back, so protest is brief and play resumes. Caregivers build this by short, predictable goodbyes with a clear return word, never sneaking out.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, neglect

rows.description: On her return the toddler may hit or turn away: the fear turned into fury. Mature response is calm welcome and naming it: you were upset when I went. Punishing the anger teaches hiding need.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, neglect, trust
related mind states: anger, fear, calm

rows.description: A child repeatedly left crying with no comfort learns that need brings nothing, and may go quiet or flat, which looks like being good. Caregivers should respond warmly and consistently; the child is never at fault.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, trust

rows.description: The child slowly borrows safety from a gentle new adult who greets warmly, holds and comforts. Wise caregivers stay a while at first, say goodbye honestly, and let the child bring a comfort toy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, neglect
